body:
## Pull request overview

Fixes the broken record-detail action execution pipeline in the console app by restoring correct action type dispatch, wiring `ActionProvider` handlers (confirm/toast/navigate/param-collection + `api` handler), and ensuring action visibility/params collection work end-to-end. Also adjusts Vercel build + Vite workspace aliasing to reliably build the console on Vercel.

**Changes:**
- Preserve original action execution type (`api`, etc.) while rendering `action:*` components, and pass record data for visibility/enabled evaluation.
- Wrap `DetailView` with a fully wired `ActionProvider`, add confirm + param collection dialogs, and implement an `api` handler backed by `dataSource.update()`.
- Add console integration tests for confirm/params/toast/update behavior; update Vercel build command and Vite aliases.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 9 out of 9 changed files in this pull request and generated 10 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-button.tsx | Uses preserved `actionType`, routes `params` vs `actionParams`, and evaluates visibility/enabled using record data. |
| packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-bar.tsx | Preserves original action type (`actionType`) while overriding component renderer type; forwards record data to inline action renderers. |
| apps/console/src/components/RecordDetailView.tsx | Adds `ActionProvider` wiring, confirm/toast/navigate/param handlers, and an `api` handler that maps action targets to `dataSource.update()`. |
| apps/console/src/components/ActionParamDialog.tsx | New dialog to collect action params based on `ActionParamDef[]`. |
| apps/console/src/components/ActionConfirmDialog.tsx | New promise-based confirm dialog using Shadcn `AlertDialog`. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/RecordDetailActions.test.tsx | New integration tests covering rendering + confirm/params/toast + `dataSource.update()` invocation. |
| apps/console/vite.config.ts | Adds missing workspace aliases for `@object-ui/mobile` and `@object-ui/plugin-designer`. |
| apps/console/vercel.json | Switches Vercel build to a Vite-only build path (no turbo prebuild), with MSW init + env flags. |
| ROADMAP.md | Documents the root causes and the implemented fixes for the record detail action chain. |
</details>

`ActionBarRenderer` now preserves the original action type via `actionType`, but only `action:button` appears to consume it. If an action uses a different `component` (e.g. `action:icon`), that renderer still executes using `schema.type` (which `action:bar` overwrites to the component type), so those actions would remain inert. Also, record `data` is passed to inline renderers but not to the overflow `action:menu`, so visibility/enabled expressions in overflow items will still evaluate without record context. Consider standardizing on `actionType` across all action renderers and forwarding `data` consistently (including overflow).

`apiHandler` declares a `_context: ActionCtx` parameter but doesn’t use it. With `noUnusedParameters: true` in `apps/console/tsconfig.json`, this will fail type-checking. Either remove the second parameter (a 1-arg function is assignable here) or use it (e.g., for record/user context).
```suggestion
  const apiHandler = useCallback(async (action: ActionDef) => {
```

Several inputs use `values[param.name] || ''`, which will coerce valid values like `0` to an empty string and lose data. Also, `number` inputs currently store `e.target.value` (string) rather than a number, and `boolean` params fall back to a text input (returning a string). Consider using nullish coalescing (`??`) for display, and normalizing value types per `param.type` (e.g., `valueAsNumber` for number, Checkbox/Switch for boolean).

`within` is imported but never used. With `noUnusedLocals: true` in the console tsconfig, this will fail type-checking for the test file. Remove the unused import (or use it).
```suggestion
import { render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
```

This assertion only checks that `update` wasn’t called with a specific argument shape; the test could still pass even if `ds.update` was called with different args. If the intent is “no update happens on cancel”, assert `expect(ds.update).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` (or check call count) to avoid false positives.
```suggestion
    expect(ds.update).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
```

Since `DetailView` renders `<SchemaRenderer schema={actionBar} data={record} />`, `action:bar` receives a `data` prop and then spreads `...rest` onto the toolbar `<div>`. That forwards an object-valued `data` prop to the DOM and can trigger React unknown-prop warnings. Consider destructuring `data` out of `props/rest` before spreading onto the `<div>` (and then explicitly passing it only to child renderers).

`data` is being read from `rest.data` but `...rest` is still spread onto the underlying Shadcn `<Button/>`, which forwards props to the DOM. Passing an object-valued `data` prop to a `<button>` will cause React unknown-prop warnings and may serialize incorrectly. Consider destructuring `data` out of `props/rest` (e.g. `const { data, ...rest } = props`) so it’s used for condition evaluation but never forwarded to the DOM element.

The `isParamDefs` check treats `schema.params` as value params unless it’s a non-empty array. But per `ActionSchema`, `params` is an array of param definitions and may be `[]`; in that case this code will pass an array into `ActionDef.params` (expected `Record<string, any>`), which can leak through to handlers / API bodies. Consider switching to `Array.isArray(schema.params) ? { actionParams: schema.params } : { params: schema.params }` and typing `actionParams` as `ActionParamDef[]` instead of `any`.
